newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM wins political breathing room.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM wins political breathing room.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda won political breathing room on Friday when an opposition leader said he would not press a no-confidence motion.
"It is a logistical problem so I'm not going to be able to press the motion," Samta Party leader George Fernandes told Reuters in the Indian capital.
The speaker of the lower house, Purno Sangma, had planned to take up Fernandes's no-confidence motion on Friday, the second day of the three-month budget session of parliament.
But on Thursday, the main opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) said it would not push for an early no-confidence motion.
"We are not interested in a no-confidence motion early in the budget session," BJP leader and former prime minister Atal Behari Vajpayee told Reuters. "We want it as the last weapon."
The Samta Party has five deputies in the 545-member Lok Sabha, or lower house of parliament. The BJP and its allies, including the Samta Party, control 194 votes.
BJP members were not scheduled to attend parliament on Friday due to a one-day mourning for a murdered deputy.
The BJP held power for 12 days in May after inconclusive general elections but was forced to step down in the face of certain defeat in a confidence vote.
Deve Gowda's 14-party United Front coalition, which assumed power last June, holds 178 votes and depends on the Congress party's 142 to survive.

Tension between Deve Gowda and Congress leader Sitaram Kesri has recently mounted. India's oldest party, which has ruled India for all but five years since independence in 1947, has sent repeated warning signals to the government not to take its support for granted.
But Congress spokesman Vithal Gadgil told Reuters on Wednesday that he expected the government to survive the budget session which is expected to end on May 12.

Gadgil's remarks were the strongest indication so far that the Congress, which suffered its worst-ever defeat in last year's general elections, was not about to precipitate the mid-term election that would follow if Deve Gowda were to lose his majority.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is due to present the budget for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) on February 28.
